# Emberveil — Prompt History

A chronological log of user prompts for this project. Brief summaries go on the public /game-info/ Prompt History section; full text lives here.

---

## 2026-04-13 — M64 queue (19 items)

1. Rework skill point system. Bubble shows 26 despite all points assigned — outdated counting. Every skill should have ≥2 talents (add generic where missing; e.g. Oracle Foresight only has Shared Vision). (a) Show remaining talent points on Skills tab matching Passive/Attributes. (b) Recalculate point awards so you can never have stranded unspendable points. Prefer consistent cadence (e.g. talent every 5 levels after level 3).
2. Ring slot: auto-assign to open slot; only prompt if replacing.
3. "Return to town through portal" button should only appear when party is standing on the portal node.
4. Replace map portal marker diamond with a blue portal icon with white outline. "Return through portal" button should use the same icon.
5. Clouds still drifting on map view — remove. Also a background band only ~6% of map height should be extended or removed.
6. Travel bug: you can switch to any map and see a party icon there. Party should only exist on 1–2 maps at a time (2 only when on the terminal node of one, enabling entry to first node of another).
7. Generate 10 new encounters that reward 10 new companions with new graphics: dire wolf, forest owl, ember drake, shadow cat, crystal golem, spirit wisp, bone hound, ice sprite, swamp frog, void moth.
8. Use ElevenLabs API + docs at ../assets/references to generate ~100 combat/spell/event SFX and ~3 music tracks (menus, combat). Descriptive prompts ("bitcrunch", "SNES-style"). Fire spells can share one fire SFX.
9. Generate 16:9 environmental background art for each map (up to 25). Photo-style OK.
10. Generate pixel-art main-menu background + cloud layers. 16:9 desktop + square mobile (use dialog bg dimensions). 2–3 cloud variations. Clouds same across devices.
11. Black market: reduce red styling. Unlock it in the town right after Enchanter unlock (next progression step).
12. Convert "Forge" from a menu tab into a town service, UI consistent with other services.
13. Fix top Merchant/Tavern/Cleric tab bar in town — currently broken; icons on main view work. Both paths should work.
14. Rename "Trophies" → "Achievements" in in-game menu.
15. Add more item variety, especially weapons.
16. Add basic starting equipment per class; replace preference text on Create Hero page (e.g. Warrior: heavy armor + 2H sword; Paladin: medium armor + scepter + shield).
17. "Disable Graphics" setting should actually skip textures and use geometric fallbacks. Add separate "Disable Backgrounds" and "Disable Sprites" toggles.
18. /demo-assets/ (and siblings) Play Game link should go to /game13/ instead of RSG Demos index.
19. Level-up reward dialog: split one character per line, show attribute/talent/passive points awarded. Every level should grant SOMETHING.

### Clarifications
- Active skills auto-unlock by level — no skill points needed, only talent points.
- Companion list confirmed; "Crystal Golem Mini" → "Crystal Golem".
- Audio cap ~100 SFX; prompts may describe style (bitcrunch, SNES).
- OpenAI for backgrounds.
- Disable Graphics → fall back to SVG/shapes; add separate toggles.
- Also update parent `claude/` new-game template so prompt history propagates automatically.

## 2026-04-13 21:42

- Change the blacksmith when upgrading quality levels to automatically roll random affixes for the new slots. 
- Style scrollbars in the game to match the theme, especially ones on the Blacksmith panel.
- On blacksmith panel remove scrollbar from each specific character, just let it be a long list and let the blacksmith UI itself scroll down - not double scrollbars.
- Add another town every 1/4/7 etc maps. Each with new random hireables at tavern. Use same criteria for unlocking blacksmith/enchanter/etc based on act. "Back to town" and town portal should go to nearest town.
- Change towns to sell random items (if not already) and towns in higher level maps should sell different, better equipment, with higher rarity, and higher quality levels esp on new game +
- Change the cleric to heal for free, revive still cost gold
- Major new system: My nephew tried playing this game with an iphone and was tapping the screen to damage enemies. I told him it didn't work that way, but I think it would be an interesting addition. Add a new town section for Tap Weapons, which store in the party's Tap Inventory (unlimited space). You can equip one tap weapon and one tap utility. When the player clicks near enemies (by proximity not click detection) the tap weapon will trigger. If you click near allies, a tap utility will be used instead. Add a variety of 10 tap weapons and 10 utilities each with their own pixellab icon and sound effects. Tap weapons/utilities can be unlocked by bosses or at special encounter dialogs if you succeed a challenging skill check. Some tap items can be used every character's turn, and others have a brief cooldown. You can only tap once per turn unless a weapon has an even longer cooldown (default: 1 turn, some may be multiple rounds). Include graphics where needed for effects and projectiles:
Some tap weapons to start with below, invent your own to fill the gaps:
-- Blade: The most basic weapon, you start with it. It damages enemies when you tap. Basically zero cooldown, not much damage.
-- Bow: Fires an arrow from off-screen to the left in an arc. If it collides with an enemy, deals significant damage. Has a medium cooldown.
-- Catapult: Fire a  boulder from off-screen similar to a bow. Deals significant area damage. Long delay (5 seconds/rounds)
-- Star Caller: Summons a falling star from above where you clicked, impacts the ground near enemies and deals area damage in an explosion. Long delay.
-- Ninja Stars: Throw 3 ninja stars from left of the screen. Deals small damage, small cooldown, can hit 3 targets or 1 target up to 3 times.
-- Fireball: Shoot a fireball from left of the screen that explodes. Deals medium damage, medium cooldown.
-- Dragon Call: Summon a dragon from left of the screen who flies overhead breathing fire, lightning, or cold on all enemy rows. Longer cooldown. Award from dragon boss.
Some tap utiltiies:
-- Rejuvenate: Apply a hot to a single target, preferring lowest HP. Medium cooldown.
-- Heal: Minor healing spell that affects a small group of allies near where you clicked. Can affect the back row or the front row. Heals 50hp split between targets. Long cooldown.
-- Shield: Adds a shield or temp hp to targets, functions like heal, barrier 25hp.
-- Deflect: Protect the target against the next attack, absorbing it completely. Affects a single target. Long cooldow.
-- Enchant: Adds bonus damage to a single target's damage and a visible indicator so you can see which one. Lasts until replaced. Short cooldown. Applying to a second target dispels the effect from the first target.
You can either use a tap weapon or utility. They share a cooldown. Otherwise you would just click left and right repeatedly and that would be crazy.
Tap weapons do not have random properties, rarity, etc. They are static, for now.
- When you reach 100 fame, next time you visit town add a dialog where an npc recognizes you and "I want you to have this" -> free rare amulet.
- When you reach 250 fame, next time you visit town add another random encounter for another rare+ loot.
- At 500 fame, one more encounter with random rare+ equipment. Unlocks the "Guild Hall" at towns. The guild hall is another vendor that sells higher rarity gear than the regular merchant, at minimum rares. There are 12 slots of gear, all random, and locked behind progressive increasing fame requirement. Fame 500 unlocks the first 3 slots. Fame 750 unlocks the 4th, etc. Higher tier slots have higher quality/rarity loot.
- Change all the new wymling, wymrm, hatchling, drake companions available at tavern to have only one be available at act 3, two at act 4, and so on until all available. There should only be a couple of companions available at each town, not all of them. Each town should have its own set of heroes at the tavern.
- Fix characters should get 2 attributes per level instead of just 1, and at level 1 you should have 8 base points plus 8 additional points spent anywhere. Heroes hired from the tavern should obey these rules, so if you buy a level 2 merc they should have 8+8+2 total skill points allocated.
- Fix the main menu fade in effect has old graphics before revealing the new background graphic. Add the background graphic earlier. Add the clouds floating in front of the background like the old non-graphic version had. Genrate pixel art for the clouds, using similar red hues from the main menu background art.
- On the main menu, add a subtle drop shadow or text shadow to the logo and subtext. Add the milestone number to the footer text on main menu. Make the footer text and subtext less transparent, the are diffeicult to read, or maybe the drop shadow/text shadow would help.

//Use this function to contact CW API
function callCloudwaysAPI($method, $url, $accessToken, $post = [])
{
    $baseURL = API_URL;
    $ch = curl_init();
    curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST, $method);
    curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_URL, $baseURL . $url);

    if ($accessToken) {
        curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, ['Authorization: Bearer ' . $accessToken]);
    }
  
    //Set Post Parameters
    $encoded = '';
    if (count($post)) {
        foreach ($post as $name => $value) {
            $encoded .= urlencode($name) . '=' . urlencode($value) . '&';
        }
        $encoded = substr($encoded, 0, strlen($encoded) - 1);
        curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, $encoded);
        curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POST, 1);
    }
    $output = curl_exec($ch);
    $httpcode = curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_HTTP_CODE);
    if ($httpcode != '200') {
        die('An error occurred code: ' . $httpcode . ' output: ' . substr($output, 0, 10000));
    }
    curl_close($ch);
    return json_decode($output);
}

//Fetch Access Token
$tokenResponse = callCloudwaysAPI('POST', '/oauth/access_token', null
    , [
    'email' => EMAIL, 
    'api_key' => API_KEY
    ]);

$accessToken = $tokenResponse->access_token;
$gitPullResponse = callCloudwaysAPI('POST', '/git/pull', $accessToken, [
    'server_id' => $_GET['server_id'],
    'app_id' => $_GET['app_id'],
    'git_url' => $_GET['git_url'],
    'branch_name' => $_GET['branch_name']
    /* Uncomment it if you want to use deploy path, Also add the new parameter in your link
    'deploy_path' => $_GET['deploy_path']  
    */    
    ]);

echo (json_encode($gitPullResponse));
?>

```js
// CombatScreen._basicAttack
let raw = actor.dmg[0] + Math.floor(Math.random() * (actor.dmg[1] - actor.dmg[0] + 1));
if (Math.random() * 100 &lt; totalCrit) { raw *= 2; isCrit = true; }
const { dmg, tag } = this._resolveIncomingDamage(raw, target, { type: 'physical' });
this._applyDamage(actor, target, dmg, color);

// _resolveIncomingDamage (new, canonical):
let dmg = Math.max(0, Math.round(raw));
let tag = null;
if (type === 'physical' &amp;&amp; (target.blockChance || 0) &gt; 0 &amp;&amp; rollBlock(target)) {
  const afterBlock = applyBlock(dmg, target);
  if (afterBlock &lt;= 0) { tag = 'blocked'; dmg = 0; }
  else { tag = `blocked ${dmg - afterBlock}`; dmg = afterBlock; }
}
const final = applyMitigation(dmg, target, { type, armorPen: opts.armorPen, resistPen: opts.resistPen });
const mitTag = mitigationLogTag(dmg, final, type);
if (mitTag) tag = mitTag;
return { dmg: final, tag };
```

## Report

**File created:** `/home/radgh/claude/game13/public/assets/skill-audit.html`

**Totals:** 82 skills audited → **~18 WIRED, ~44 PARTIAL, ~20 ORPHAN** (≈22% fully wired). On top of that, **~144 talents + ~144 upgrade tiers are globally orphaned** — `CombatScreen._executeSkill` never merges `skill.talents[].effect` or `skill.upgrades[].bonus` before casting. The player picks them in UI; combat runs untalented base.

**Root causes (not per-skill bugs):**
1. Talents &amp; upgrades never merged into the skill at cast time.
2. `aoe` dictionary only handles `single/adjacent/group/row/all`. Every exotic value (`chain, chain3, random3, multi3, pierce_row, single_overflow, adjacent2, group2, row2`) falls through to single target.
3. `eff.extraAction` is SET on target but NEVER READ by the turn loop.
4. `type:zone/trap/counter/utility/debuff/passive` all unhandled — fall through to damage path.
5. `_getSkillStat` missing `dex_int`, `dex_con` — silently falls back to STR.
6. `reflect / lifesteal / armorPen / bonusVsUndead / bonusVsDemon` never read anywhere.
7. Nine type:buff skills have **no `effect` object at all**: Sanctuary, Inspiring Tune, Ballad of Valor, Soul Pact, Fel Sight, Dragon Scales, Draconic Fury, Taunt, Poison Blade — they do literally nothing.

**Per-class worst offenders:**
- **Chronomancer: 0 of 4 wired.** Haste (ORPHAN), Slow Time (PARTIAL — only 40% INT damage; signature "enemies lose actions" dead), Rewind (PARTIAL — cleanse dead), Time Stop (ORPHAN — 70 MP and neither `extraAction` nor `enemySkipRound` fires). **User's suspicion is 100% confirmed.**
- **Tactician: 2 of 4 wired** (Rally Action ORPHAN, Masterstroke PARTIAL — extra-action payload dead).
- **Bard: 1 of 4** (3 skills are missing effect objects entirely).
- **Dragon Knight: 1 of 4** (Dragon Scales &amp; Draconic Fury missing effect objects).
- **Scavenger: 0 of 4** (all either unknown type or missing statuses/stats).
- **Swashbuckler: 0 of 4** (Riposte type:counter unhandled, Taunt no effect, Flourish/Grandeur rely on nonexistent Flair system).

**Top 5 most surprising orphans:**
1. **Haste (Chronomancer)** — unread key `effect.extraAction`. Claims ally acts again; ally never does.
2. **Time Stop (Chronomancer)** — unread `effect.extraAction` + `effect.enemySkipRound`. 70 MP ultimate that does absolutely nothing.
3. **Magic Missile (Mage)** — `aoe:random3` falls through to single. "Launch 3 bolts" actually fires 1 bolt at 1 target.
4. **Second Wind (Fighter)** — unread `healAmount: 80`. Heal path uses `healMult*INT`; with no mult defined the skill heals ~1.5×INT, not 80.
5. **Life Drain (Necromancer)** — unread `lifesteal: 0.5`. The Necromancer's sustain fantasy is a no-op; caster never heals from damage dealt.

Honorable mentions: Sanctuary, Inspiring Tune, Ballad of Valor, Soul Pact, Dragon Scales, Draconic Fury, Fel Sight, Taunt, Poison Blade all have no `effect` object and do nothing at all. Chain Lightning, Multi-Shot, Thunder Ring all hit 1 enemy.

**Chronomancer suspicion: CONFIRMED AND WORSE THAN EXPECTED.** 3 of 4 Chronomancer skills are broken; 2 are fully orphaned including the level-15 ultimate. The root cause (`extraAction` never consumed by turn loop) also silently breaks Tactician, Bard, and parts of Cleric. _From skill-audit.html — game13_

## Root causes (fix first — unblocks ~90% of orphans)

1. **Talents never apply.** `_executeSkill` (CombatScreen.js:~1034) gets raw `SKILLS[id]`. Add `mergeSkillWithTalents(skill, memberTalentIds)` that deep-merges each selected talent's `.effect` onto the skill before cast.

Repairs Cleave, Magic Missile, Multi-Shot, Chain Lightning, Thunder Ring, Bone Spike, Pyroclasm, Arcane Surge in one change.

# Report

## Phase A (Warrior test) — BLOCKED, no credits spent

**Starting balance:** 4,018 credits (note: this is 4k, not the ~10k the plan assumed — 80% cap = 3,214 spend ceiling).

**What happened:** I never got a successful `/keyframes` submission. The endpoint's real schema contradicts the previous agent's notes. Progressive 400 responses revealed:

1. `render_mode` is required (`"pixel"` or `"detailed"`) — not documented in the notes.
2. `frames` must be a **non-empty array** of keyframe anchors.
3. Each `frames[i]` requires `index` (integer) AND `image`/`image_url`.
4. `total_frames` is the **total length of the output sequence** that the supplied keyframes anchor — not "how many distinct variants to generate."

**Interpretation:** `/keyframes` is keyframe-conditioned **animation interpolation** (you supply frame 0 and frame N as anchors, API fills in the tween). It is NOT a "give me 6 different poses from one portrait" endpoint. `/animate` is similar — image → motion sequence from a single anchor.

**Neither endpoint supports the `total_frames: 6 → 6 distinct poses` workflow the plan assumed.** The 24-credit/char optimization is a mirage; it was based on a misreading of the docs. # Skill Rewiring Plan

_From skill-audit.html — game13_

## Root causes (fix first — unblocks ~90% of orphans)

1. **Talents never apply.** `_executeSkill` (CombatScreen.js:~1034) gets raw `SKILLS[id]`. Add `mergeSkillWithTalents(skill, memberTalentIds)` that deep-merges each selected talent's `.effect` onto the skill before cast.
2. **Upgrades never apply.** Same fix: deep-merge highest unlocked `upgrades[].bonus` tier by character level.
3. **aoe dictionary incomplete.** Add branches for `adjacent2, random3, multi3, chain, chain3, pierce_row, single_overflow, group2, row2`, reading `bolts/chainTargets/chainCount/targets`. Repairs Cleave, Magic Missile, Multi-Shot, Chain Lightning, Thunder Ring, Bone Spike, Pyroclasm, Arcane Surge in one change.
4. **`_getSkillStat` missing combined stats.** Add `dex_int`, `dex_con`. Demon Hunter/Scavenger currently fall back to STR silently.
5. **Type branches missing.** Implement `zone, trap, counter, utility, debuff, passive` (or route them).
6. **`extraAction` orphaned in turn loop.** Make the turn scheduler consume `actor.extraAction` to grant another slot. Unbreaks Rally Action, Haste, Masterstroke, Time Stop, Ballad of Valor — root of the user's Chronomancer complaint.
7. **`enemySkipRound` / `actionsLost` never read.** Wire into enemy turn-scheduler (Slow Time, Time Stop).
8. **`reflect / lifesteal / armorPen / bonusVsUndead / bonusVsDemon` never read.** Wire into `_resolveIncomingDamage / _applyDamage`.
9. **Missing `effect` objects on these buff skills (type:buff with no effect → buff branch iterates nothing):** Sanctuary, Inspiring Tune, Ballad of Valor, Soul Pact, Fel Sight, Dragon Scales, Draconic Fury, Taunt, Poison Blade.
10. **Missing `statusEffects` arrays:** Entangle, Hellfire, Glaive Toss, Thrown Junk, Makeshift Bomb, Nature's Wrath.

Separating the game from marketing content is essential for organic discovery of both.&lt;/li&gt;
```html
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Canonical URLs Are Non-Optional for Multi-Domain Setup&lt;/strong&gt; — With GitHub Pages serving a subdomain (&lt;code&gt;radgh.github.io/RSG-Demos/game13&lt;/code&gt;) and a custom domain, canonical URLs prevent duplicate content penalties and ensure ranking consolidation.&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;LLMs.txt is Worth Adopting Early&lt;/strong&gt; — The emerging llmstxt.org standard provides a lightweight, human-readable site summary for LLM context windows. This is likely to become as important as robots.txt for search bots in the next 18 months.&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Featured Images Dramatically Improve Share Quality&lt;/strong&gt; — Open Graph image metadata, when paired with compelling hero imagery from the game, increases click-through rates on social media by 3-5x based on external testing.&lt;/li&gt;

      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Schema.org Validation&lt;/strong&gt; — Tested VideoGame structured data markup using Google's Rich Results Test to ensure proper parsing&lt;/li&gt;
      &lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Link Auditing&lt;/strong&gt; — Verified all internal links, header navigation, and footer links point to correct canonical URLs&lt;/li&gt;
```

```
  --auto-corners --tolerance 40
```

## 2026-04-21 23:38

I want to work on a major rebalance overhaul. I want to be able to easily revert back, and I want you to be able to list different versions we can revert to. Ideally the rebalance changes are basically like a mod that overwrites the default settings so they can just be dropped in and tested.

Here is a prompt I generated to help streamline it:

Target: game13/ (Emberveil — existing game, rebalance initiative)
Game key: game13
Milestone: M1 of a four-milestone rebalance arc — config extraction + reversibility

Context (read carefully before doing anything):
game13 is the most-active game in the workspace. It is playable, has a full
progression loop (tavern → Acts → combat → loot → level up), and uses an
attribute/affix system with on-hit triggers and durations. The problem: it's
too easy. A solo level-1 character with no gear can reach Act 3. The user
wants to rebalance aggressively, but wants all balance changes REVERSIBLE via
config swap, so "revert to current behavior" is a one-line change.

The rebalance has four parts, each its own milestone:
  - M1 (THIS ONE): Extract all balance-affecting numbers into swappable JSON
    config files. No behavior changes yet — baseline config must reproduce
    current game behavior EXACTLY. Reversibility is the whole point.
  - M2: Build a headless full-run simulator CLI that plays through a run
    end-to-end using hand-coded policies (balanced, greedy-damage,
    greedy-tank). Report death rates per policy over 100 runs.
  - M3: Implement the armor DR rework (additive stacking, 95% cap, WoW-ish
    curve for armor-to-DR conversion) and add the Tap Power affix (scales
    tap-weapon damage AND utility-slot magnitude/duration). Both as new
    config entries; baseline config keeps old behavior.
  - M4: Iterate numeric values (hero prices, enemy stats, drop rates, armor
    curve constants, Tap Power tiers) until simulator reports: balanced
    policy ~25% death rate, greedy-damage 40%+, greedy-tank ~15%. Ship the
    resulting config as the new active default; keep baseline as a named
    preset for revert.

M1 SCOPE — what you are doing this cycle:

Step 1: Investigation (report findings before touching code).
Grep game13's source for every balance-affecting number. At minimum:
  - Hero costs at the tavern (L1 and L2 custom heroes + companion heroes)
  - Enemy base stats per Act (HP, damage, armor, any scaling formulas)
  - Drop rates and loot table weights
  - Gold income (encounter rewards, shop prices, chest contents)
  - Character stat derivations (HP per level, damage per stat point, etc.)
  - Armor → damage formula (current flat-subtraction system)
  - Tap weapon damage + utility slot effect magnitudes/durations
  - Any XP / leveling curves
  - Any existing affix values (damage %, HP %, etc.)

Produce a file: game13/memory/rebalance-m1-audit.md listing every number
found, its current value, source file:line, and a brief note on what it
controls. This is the inventory we're extracting.

IMPORTANT: Before producing the audit, ALSO report:
  - What does game13's existing in-game combat simulator look like? Where
    does its code live? Is combat logic already separated from UI, or is it
    entangled with render/animation code? (This is critical for M2 — the
    sim harness needs pure combat logic.)
  - Is there any randomness in combat? Is it already seeded, or does it use
    Math.random? (M2 will need seeded RNG; flagging scope now helps.)
  - Does the user's mention of "tap weapons" vs "utility slots" match the
    code's terminology? If not, what's the actual naming?

Report these findings to the user and pause for review BEFORE starting Step 2.
Do NOT guess or proceed if anything is unclear.

Step 2: Config extraction architecture.

Create a directory: game13/public/data/balance/
  - balance.baseline-2026-04-21.json — snapshot of CURRENT values, verbatim
  - balance.active.json — starts as an exact copy of baseline; this is what
    the game reads at runtime
  - README.md — explains the swap mechanism and lists named presets

The game code reads balance values from balance.active.json. No other config
file. To revert: copy baseline-2026-04-21.json over active.json. To try a
variant: save active.json under a new named preset, swap in the variant.
That's the whole mechanism — keep it stupid.

Schema: organize by domain, not by file.
{
  "version": "2026-04-21-baseline",
  "heroes": {
    "tavernPrices": { "level1Custom": <n>, "level2Custom": <n>, "companion": <n> },
    "startingStats": { ... },
    ...
  },
  "combat": {
    "armorFormula": { "type": "flat-subtraction", "params": { ... } },
    "damageReductionCap": <n>,
    ...
  },
  "enemies": { "act1": { ... }, "act2": { ... }, "act3": { ... } },
  "economy": { "encounterGoldRange": [n, n], "shopMarkup": <n>, ... },
  "affixes": { "existingAffixes": [ ... ], "tapPower": null },
  "dropRates": { ... },
  "progression": { "xpCurve": [ ... ], "statPointsPerLevel": <n>, ... }
}

The structure does NOT need to match internal code structure. In fact, it
SHOULDN'T — code internals will change over time; the config should reflect
the designer's mental model. A loader module maps config → internal values at
startup.

Step 3: Wire it up.

Create game13/src/balance-loader.js (or wherever fits the project's
structure — check the code layout first). This module:
  - Fetches balance.active.json at game boot.
  - Exposes a typed getter API: balance.heroes.tavernPrices.level1Custom,

## 2026-04-26 17:18

From brainstorm.html:

I picked the following 74 feature(s) from the Emberveil brainstorm at /assets/brainstorm.html. Please plan and implement them in upcoming milestone(s).

## 1. Screen-by-screen UX audit

- **Unified Spells / Passives / Attributes / Inventory tabbed panel** _[medium, ui]_ — Reduce screen count; quick item swaps during skill-point allocation flow.
- **Rename map "Inventory" button to "Party" (opens unified Party + Inventory)** _[medium, ui]_ — Clearer intent; collapses the Inventory + Town notification-bubble overlap.
- **Notification bubble disambiguation: Inventory tab gets bubble for unequipped/upgrades; map Town button shows level-up points only** _[small, ui]_ — Eliminates the misleading "skill points available" bubble on the map Inventory button.
- **Quick-equip toast on item pickup** _[small, ui]_ — Show "Auto-equipped X to Y" or "X is an upgrade for Z — equip?" when loot drops, so the player doesn't have to open inventory after every fight.
- **Combat preview tooltip on skill upgrade selection** _[small, ui]_ — "This upgrade adds N% damage / changes targeting to AoE" — contextual hint when picking talents.
- **Scroll-position memory on InventoryScreen tab switch** _[small, ui]_ — Preserve scroll depth when jumping between characters.
- **MapScreen zone fast-travel as dropdown (not tabs)** _[medium, ui]_ — Reduce horizontal width on phones once 6+ zones are unlocked.
- **Status effect tooltips show duration remaining (not just type)** _[small, ui]_ — Players can't tell when burns / blocks expire without counting rounds.
- **Dual-comparison mode in Inventory (compare both rings / offhand at once)** _[small, ui]_ — Better multi-slot planning.
- **Party screen role icons (Tank / DPS / Support / Healer)** _[small, ui]_ — Visual scan vs reading stats.
- **Boss-intro splash card before boss combat** _[medium, ui]_ — Sells the moment; differentiates from regular fights.

## 2. New gameplay elements

- **Multi-phase boss fights (HP checkpoints unlock new attack patterns)** _[large, combat]_ — Generalize the Unraveler pattern to 3-5 other final bosses.
- **Companion level-sync option (scale companion to party avg)** _[small, gameplay]_ — Reduce friction when swapping companions mid-act.
- **Flee from combat (DEX check; failure costs gold)** _[medium, combat]_ — Recovery option early-act instead of auto-wipe.
- **Steal-buff mechanic (Rogue) — pull enemy buffs to self** _[small, combat]_ — New effect type; high-skill play.
- **Bleed-stack burst finisher skill** _[medium, combat]_ — Make bleed-focused builds rewarding beyond passive DoT.
- **Curse system (negative buff that spreads on death)** _[medium, combat]_ — Differentiate curses from poison/burn; Warlock identity.
- **New node type: Travelling merchant (stops on the path; one-time stock)** _[medium, gameplay]_ — Adds urgency / decision moment outside of towns.
- **New node type: Skill check (single attribute roll, success/fail branches)** _[small, gameplay]_ — More variety than combat/dialog; rewards stat investment.

## 3. New content

- **40 new affixes (elemental combos, conditional triggers, set bonuses)** _[large, content]_ — Deepen itemization beyond the current ~30 affixes.
- **Boss-themed loot tables (e.g. Unraveler always drops void-themed items)** _[medium, content]_ — Memorable rewards for memorable fights.
- **Craftable unique items (5/act, recipe unlocks on boss kill)** _[medium, content]_ — Bridge merchant/blacksmith/enchanter workflows.
- **Hidden boss encounters (gated by rare-loot-finds or stat thresholds)** _[medium, content]_ — Easter eggs for completionists / speedrunners.
- **8 new dialogue branches per act (gated on party comp / past choices)** _[large, content]_ — Replay value; story is mostly linear today.
- **Procedural challenge dungeon (random Act 1-4 enemies + twists)** _[medium, content]_ — Replayable post-game content for build-testing.

## 4. Expansions to existing features

- **Crafting recipe unlocks via lore-node exploration** _[medium, content]_ — Make Blacksmith/Enchanter discovery dynamic instead of static stock.
- **Hardcore monument on title screen (display fallen heroes)** _[medium, content]_ — Honor losses; community feature.
- **Fame-locked appearance / weapon variety unlocks** _[medium, content]_ — Long-term carrot; fame is invisible today.
- **Enchanter upgrade preview (before/after stats on hover)** _[small, ui]_ — Half-done per CLAUDE.md; finalize the tooltip.
- **Potion belt (combat-quick consumables, separate from inventory)** _[medium, ui]_ — QoL for healing flow; UX win.
- **Boss-specific dialogue preludes (every boss gets a 2-3 line intro)** _[small, content]_ — Sells stakes; cheap content.

## 5. Accessibility

- **Colorblind palettes (deuteranopia / protanopia / tritanopia)** _[medium, accessibility]_ — Rarity colors today are red/blue/yellow/orange — collide for ~8% of players.
- **Font-size scaling (Settings → 80%/100%/120%/150%)** _[medium, accessibility]_ — Fixed 1rem today; mobile readability win.
- **Keyboard navigation across screens (arrow + enter)** _[large, accessibility]_ — Mouse/touch only today; unblocks desktop power users + a11y users.
- **Tap-target validation (all buttons ≥ 44×44px per WCAG)** _[medium, accessibility]_ — Many tooltip-trigger areas likely undersized on mobile.
- **Reduce-motion toggle (kill parallax, screen wipes)** _[medium, accessibility]_ — Already partial; expand coverage.
- **Plain-language status descriptions (not just icon names)** _[small, accessibility]_ — Cognitive accessibility; avoid jargon.
- **Subtitle / caption mode for combat log** _[medium, accessibility]_ — Screen-reader friendly real-time combat narration.

## 6. Claude-driven simulators & benchmarks

- **Headless combat simulator API (spawn combatants, run N rounds, return stats)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Currently Monte Carlo lives in scripts; expose as a clean Node API for Claude to call.
- **Batch rebalance reports (test 50 skill tweaks in parallel, compare win-rates)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Currently serial; parallelize + CSV export.
- **Automated end-to-end playthrough (seeded RNG, full Act 1-4 run, softlock detection)** _[large, devtool]_ — Smoke test after balance changes.
- **Regression alerts on rebalance (alert if Act 1 win-rate drops >10%)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Safety net; currently manual comparison.
- **Item-generation validator (every affix rolls within bounds)** _[small, devtool]_ — Catch balance bugs early.
- **Affix coverage report (which affixes never appear in Act 1-2 loot)** _[small, devtool]_ — Identify dead content; gap analysis.
- **Combat-log replayer (save fight trace JSON, replay visually on demand)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Debug tool; invaluable for balance QA.
- **Status-effect interaction matrix (all 2-effect combos, computed outcomes)** _[small, devtool]_ — Identify unintended synergies.
- **Encounter difficulty rating (predicted win-rate, flag too-hard fights)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Proactive balance feedback; uses simulator.
- **Save-file load-tester (load 100 random saves, check for crashes)** _[small, devtool]_ — Prevent save-corruption regressions.
- **Loot distribution audit (drop chance per act; flag rare over-drop)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Balance economy beyond gut-check.

## 7. Website & dev tools audit

- **Companion catalog page (sortable table: name, class, stats, skills)** _[small, devtool]_ — Missing entirely; companions are semi-documented in code only.
- **Dungeon catalog page (location, stages, mini-boss, rewards)** _[small, devtool]_ — Data lives in mapData.js; expose for designers.
- **Status effect catalog page (full glossary, sources, interactions)** _[small, devtool]_ — No public reference exists.
- **Affix interaction matrix page (which stack / conflict / multiply)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Critical for balance; no visual map today.
- **Achievement roadmap page (prerequisites, unlock conditions, rarity)** _[small, devtool]_ — Help players chase trophies.
- **Skill interaction simulator (test "skill A + skill B" combo)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Useful for balance design.
- **image-review-manifest deprecation pass (1.6 MB; stale entries)** _[medium, devtool]_ — Clean it up.
- **character-redesign archive (preserve old versions, currently overwritten)** _[small, devtool]_ — Design history.
- **wishlist.html: group by milestone target** _[small, devtool]_ — Currently flat list; hard to prioritise.
- **Spell catalog: side-by-side skill comparison** _[medium, devtool]_ — Helps streamline talent design.
- **Rebalance report diff view (old → new highlighted)** _[small, devtool]_ — Currently fresh report each time; hard to spot changes.
- **Asset-pipeline trace tool (which scripts touch which files)** _[small, devtool]_ — Reduce confusion on stale workflows.
- **Tools-menu landing page (replace bare /assets/ index with curated table)** _[small, devtool]_ — Discoverability for the 15+ tools that already exist.

## 8. Milestone / changelog / news flow

- **In-game "What's New?" splash on first launch after update** _[medium, content]_ — Engage players with patch notes; currently external only.
- **Changelog categorization (Bug Fix / Feature / Balance / QoL / Art icons)** _[small, content]_ — Improve scannability; flat lists are hard.
- **Per-feature "shipped in M###" badge (visible at the feature itself)** _[small, content]_ — Celebrate; drive engagement ("new in M291!").
- **Public roadmap page (upcoming acts, major features)** _[medium, content]_ — Manage expectations; hype building.
- **"Patch notes" shortcut in GameMenu (link to latest release summary)** _[small, ui]_ — Discoverability without leaving the game.
- **Achievement-unlock toast notifications** _[small, ui]_ — Celebration moment; currently silent unlock.
- **Boss-defeat cinematic dialog (capture story beat, not just combat)** _[large, content]_ — Leverage story; minimal boss dialog today.
- **In-game lore compendium (unlocked as you discover lore nodes)** _[medium, content]_ — Help follow the 4-act narrative.
- **Backward-compat notes on release (flag breaking saves, migration info)** _[small, devtool]_ — Reduce confusion when mechanics change.
- **Versioned asset archive (snapshot per milestone for archaeology)** _[small, devtool]_ — Preserve design history; valuable for postmortems.
- **release.sh prompt for changelog category tags** _[small, devtool]_ — Force categorization at release time so the player-facing changelog organizes itself.
- **public/news/ folder + rotating "Latest News" widget on the asset gallery** _[medium, content]_ — A place for non-changelog announcements (events, dev diaries).

When you start, group by milestone (small items first), confirm scope before opening tickets that need design discussion, and follow the no-silent-shelving rule from CLAUDE.md.

Manual additions:
1. Need to fix after levelling up in combat you see what skills were auto upgraded, but the bubble count of unspent skill points still shows up until you visit character screen.
2. For dual comparison mode noted above: Consider iphone probably won't be able to fix that on one screen so consider using this only for desktop.
3. For party screen role icons: Remember no emoji. SVG are fine. Font Awesome is also available, but I like teh current class icons that were generated too and we can continue that style.
4. Boss intro cards: Reminds me the bosses with a long name have their name intro get cut off especially on iphone, need to respond to screen width or wrap.
5. Companion level sync: I think the party average level has potential too and can be displayed on save games etc.
6. Bleed stack: Bleed, poison, and other DoT spells should have the option to allow stacking from the same character, or one stack per characer, or one stack from any source. However works best into the current system.
7. Enemy Spells: It's time we start adding some spells to enemies in the game. They will need new artwork, but as long as fallbacks are used that's no problem. Let's add spells to some enemies in the game, but keep many basic monsters who just auto attack (especially goblins). Bosses could have wind-up spells that can be interrupted by dealing sufficient damage or dispelling/spell stealing a buff, etc. You might be able to steal very powerful buffs from some bosses that change the tide of combat.
8. Add modifiers to enemies like Diablo 2 when you fight an enemy with a blue name who has benefits like health regeneration or an aura. This can tie into enemy spells. I'm also thinking of Silk Road Online where you could fight a giant fiery version of a monster like a mini-boss, rare events probably best reserved to "Challenge" tiles.
9. Travelling Merchant: I'm thinking this node type can be similar to Mario Bros 3 where there is a rigid map, but there can randomly be minigames like the memory game, which appear over a node. These can be bonus levels and can be positive minigames or neutral ones like travelling merchant or hostile encounters like bandit patrol. It can also tie in to quest system.
10. Set bonuses: I love set items. Let's add set items. Not just end game but like Diablo 2's Sigon armor there should be low level sets too that have powerful modifiers not found on regular gear. Ideally they could have "legendary effects" like Diablo 3 for example a Mage set could make Magic Missile release projectiles against another target as a bonus AoE. We could also add unique items that are basically rare items with a legendary effect (or rarely, multiple). Unique and set items should be pre-determined legendary effects, may have pre-determined affixes or be entirely random. All affixes should still be random values unless specified in the item template (Sigon Shield could be designed to always give +5 STR for example).
11. On the brainstorm.html update all the items I selected to be moved to a new "Approved" section, and move them to wishlist.html for tracking. They should no longer be selectable on the brainstorm.html page and can be illustrated by a checkmark.
12. Crafting recipe unlock: Make it easy to unlock all basic/white recipes.
13. Hardcore Monument: Only displayed if a hardcore character has fallen.
14. Reduce motion toggle: Add to menu if it's not there (My OS has this enabled and IDK how to change it, assuming others too)
15. Regression Alerts: I'd like to also be able to adjust the settings for example having Act 5 win rate 25% instead of 10% etc (just example, don't implement)
16. We should also audit numbers in the DPS meter and attributes to prevent rounding issues (13.000000001%). Most stats like HP/MP/STR can be floored to simplify. Some stats like crit chance should remain float. Etc. You decide.
17. Save file load tester: Along with the ability to run a full playthrough, you should automatically save a game afterwards for each milestone version. You can use those to test for regression issue later, as just an example. If you already had something in mind, go with that This is just a suggestion.
18. Loot distribution: Also should account for merchant, guild hall, black market.
19. All website tools: Ensure these tools use real game data and/or allow overrides. I'm concerned these tools will become outdated and stale.

You will be acting autonomously to implement all of these features, using as many milestones as needed. Deploy after each milestone, maintain checklists, and do not let any features slip through the cracked unnoticed.

## Combat Debugging — implementation report

### Files

- **Created:** `/home/radgh/claude/game13/src/utils/combatDebug.js` — structured event logger + ring buffer (5000 entries cap), `parseDamageFromLogLine` helper, `checkParity` cross-check, `window.__combatDebug` mirror, O(1) early-bail when disabled.
- **Edited:** `/home/radgh/claude/game13/src/ui/screens/SettingsScreen.js` — imported combatDebug helpers, re-exported `isCombatDebugLogging`, added the "Combat Debugging" toggle row right after "Debug Mode", wired its click handler. Persists via `localStorage.emberveil_combat_debug_log`.
- **Edited:** `/home/radgh/claude/game13/src/ui/screens/CombatScreen.js` — instrumentation, parity check, telemetry, and post-combat notice/copy button.

### Numbers

- **20** `combatDebug.push(...)` call sites added (plus 9 context/group/clear/checkParity helper calls).
- 1 telemetry event added (`combat_summary`, gated by `isAnalyticsEnabled()`), summary-only, max 8 source entries.

### 5 most useful event kinds (where bugs surface)

1. **`meter_add`** — wraps every `_meterAddDamage/Heal/Mit/Dodge`. Records the literal `source` string + type + element + `legendary` flag. This is the exact site where the M369 Dragon-Breath-bucketed-as-Attack bug originated.
2. **`damage_apply` / `damage_apply_enter`** — pre-mitigation raw + post-mitigation final, with full breakdown (barrier absorb, DR absorb, marked amp, soulbind split, overkill). Lets you reconcile what the log line says vs what HP actually moved.
3. **`legendary_proc`** — every `_dispatchLegendaryHook` records hook name, owning actor, effect IDs, ctx (target/dealt/crit). Pinpoints which legendary fired and what attribution it passed in.
4. **`hit_check` / `crit_check`** — every roll vs threshold for basic attacks, including blind/dazed modifiers. Catches "why did I miss/crit" disputes.
5. **`parity_warning`** — emitted by the new end-of-combat cross-check (meter vs report vs parsed log lines, 5% tolerance). This is the canary that surfaces attribution bugs without anyone reading 5000 events.

### Resistant code

- The skill execution path (`_executeSkill`) is huge (~600 lines, many branches: heal/buff/aoe/chain/revive/etc.). Rather than add 50 push calls inside, instrumentation taps the choke points (`skill_cast_attempt` at entry from `_heroAI`, then `_applyDamage`/`_applyStatus`/`_meterAddDamage` which every skill funnels through). Same approach for `_basicAttack` — instrumented at the funnel functions, not every micro-branch.
- The enemy spell wind-up path emits `_log_` lines but no separate hook; those are caught via the `log_line` mirror inside `_log_`.
- No minified/obfuscated paths encountered.

### Settings UI behavior

- Toggle off by default, no perf cost when off (`if (!this.enabled) return` is the first line of every public method).
- Persists across reloads via `localStorage.emberveil_combat_debug_log = '1'`.
- Hint text matches the spec verbatim.

### Post-combat UX

- When debug is on AND a parity warning fired, both Victory and Defeat modals get a red-bordered notice "⚠ Combat parity mismatch — open console for details" plus a "Copy Debug Log" button that puts `JSON.stringify(combatDebug.buffer, null, 2)` on the clipboard. Buffer always available at `window.__combatDebug.buffer` for DevTools inspection.

### Telemetry

- `_runCombatParityCheck(outcome)` runs at start of `_victory()`, `_defeat()`, and the success branch of `_attemptFlee()`. Emits a single `combat_summary` GA/Supabase event (encounter_name, outcome, rounds, party/enemy totals, parity_warnings, legendary_procs, top-8 source_breakdown, act). Skips entirely when `isAnalyticsEnabled()` is false; skips compute work when both debug+analytics are off.

### Tests

- `npx vitest run` → **20 files passed, 277/277 tests pass** in 4.6s. No regressions.

### Not committed/deployed

## Combat Debug Playtest — Report

**Runs:** 25 combats (5 encounters × 5 seeds), **6,089 events** synthesized.

**Top 3 most actionable findings:**

1. **Critical structural gap — sim/screen share zero code paths.** `grep -n combatDebug src/game/simulator.js` returns nothing; all 20 instrumentation call sites live only in `CombatScreen.js`. The user's stated goal ("compare sim vs screen for same seed") is currently **structurally impossible**. The simulator reimplements `runSimulation` independently from CombatScreen's `_advanceTurn` / `_executeSkill` / `_applyDamage`. Fix: instrument simulator with the same `combatDebug.push` sites, OR extract a shared core.

2. **Simulator does not invoke legendary procs.** `runSimulation` (simulator.js:486-627) never calls `dispatchLegendaryHook`. The exact M369 Dragon Breath bug class — legendary proc bucketed under "Attack" — is undetectable headless. `balance-snapshot.cjs` therefore cannot validate any new legendary effect.

3. **No status_tick events from sim.** simulator.js:507-516 silently decrements buff durations. 22 `status_no_ticks` findings raised across runs. DoT damage attribution (poison/burn/bleed) cannot be parity-checked.

**Sim vs screen divergence reproducible?** No — but only because **the harness cannot run the screen path at all**. CombatScreen is heavily DOM/canvas coupled (`this._spawnDmgNumber`, `this._flashMap`, `this._el`...). The 0 parity warnings reported by the harness are an artifact of synthesizing meter/apply/log from a single sim log array — by construction they match. To get real warnings the next agent must either instrument the sim or use the documented DevTools recipe (live combat → `copy(JSON.stringify(window.__combatDebug.buffer))` → drop into `public/assets/data/combat-debug/live-*.json`).

**Secondary signal:** at L12 with act-2-tier gear, the test party loses 60–100% of regular fights and 100% of bosses in sim. May be a real balance regression vs M321 numbers, or a party-build artifact — flagged for next agent.

- Per-encounter data: `/home/radgh/claude/game13/public/assets/data/combat-debug/{goblin_camp,corrupted_outpost,obsidian_garrison,archfiend_malgrath,dragon_king_fight}.json`
- Aggregate: `/home/radgh/claude/game13/public/assets/data/combat-debug/_findings.json`

- `/home/radgh/claude/game13/src/game/simulator.js` — added combatDebug instrumentation (~16 push sites), legendary hook dispatch (onCombatStart/onHit/onCrit/onKill/onCast), per-source damage meter (`damageBySource`), per-round status ticks via shared `statusTick.js`, and a `simCtx` shared between AI/skill/legendary code paths.
- `/home/radgh/claude/game13/src/game/statusTick.js` — **new** shared module exporting `computeStatusTick(status)` and `isDotStatus(type)`. Mirrors CombatScreen's burn/bleed/poison (DoT) and regen formulas.
- `/home/radgh/claude/game13/scripts/combat-debug-replay.cjs` — enables `combatDebug` at boot, equips the warrior with a 2-piece Dragon-Lord's Aspect (dragon_fury_breath legendary) and the mage with 2-piece Apprentice Initiation (mage_missile_aoe), reads `combatDebug.buffer` into per-run `realCounts`, and surfaces the new `damageBySource` breakdown.

### combatDebug.push sites added in simulator
~16 distinct sites: `initiative_roll`, `turn_order`, `turn_start`, `ai_decision`, `skill_cast_attempt`, `hit_check` (skill + basic-attack paths), `crit_check`, `damage_calc` (skill + basic-attack), `damage_apply` (skill + basic-attack + legendary shim), `meter_add` (skill + basic-attack + legendary shim), `status_apply` (legendary shim), `status_tick` (DoT + regen), `legendary_proc` (one per dispatched hook), `report_finalize`. All gated by `combatDebug.enabled`; benchmark = **167ms for 1000 runs with cdb disabled** (no regression — push() returns at the first `if` guard).

### Legendary procs fire and meter-attribute correctly
goblin_camp run 0 (warrior on Dragon-Lord's Aspect 2-piece, mage on Apprentice Initiation 2-piece) emitted **47 `legendary_proc` events** and the per-source meter for War shows `{"Whirlwind":115,"Cleave":223,"Dragon Breath":120}` — Dragon Breath is bucketed as its own source (M369 attribution rule honored), not folded into Cleave or Attack. Sequence: Cleave's `damage_apply` → kill → `legendary_proc{hook:onKill,effectIds:["dragon_fury_breath"]}` → multiple `damage_apply{source:"Dragon Breath",legendary:true}` + `meter_add{source:"Dragon Breath"}` for each surviving enemy.

### Status ticks fire and apply damage
goblin_camp run 0 emitted **4 `status_apply` + 8 `status_tick`** events with per-tick damage applied (e.g. `bleed` from `crit_bleed_5` legendary, plus `burn` from `dragon_fury_breath`'s status side-effect). Status-tick damage is logged as a `status_tick` log entry on each round.

**None.** All 277 tests across 20 files pass on the first try, including `balance.test.js`. Win rates and avg-rounds match the pre-change snapshot reported in the playtest doc (e.g. goblin_camp 0%/9.0 rounds, corrupted_outpost 40%/12.0 rounds, dragon_king 0%/2.6 rounds). The reason thresholds didn't drift: `balance.test.js` parties carry no `setId` on equipment, so `_legendaryEffectIds` is `[]` and dispatch is a no-op; legendary procs only activate when item set membership is set, which the harness now does explicitly.

**1. Mode selection — Settings toggle + pre-combat toast**
Settings is the right home because the player may want to switch mid-campaign, not just before a specific fight. A 2-second non-blocking toast at combat start replaces any modal confirmation gate. **3. Turn lifecycle state machine**
Four states: `IDLE → DISPATCH → AWAITING-INPUT → RESOLVING → IDLE`. The key insertion point is `update(dt)` — a single guard `if (this._awaitingInput) return` before the `_turnTimer` accumulator freezes the loop entirely. `_pauseForPlayerInput(actor)` sets the flag and returns; `_dispatchManualAction` clears it. One nullable field is the source of truth, not per-character booleans. The phase 06 contract is written out explicitly as a five-condition button-hot formula, including the `hasSilence` runtime check.

The two splice-back mechanisms (`:2549` for `extraAction`, `:2559` for `_speedExtraRemaining`) are replaced by a single while-loop drain called during RESOLVING. Combat-end is unchanged; documented with `_checkCombatEnd()` called at the tail of RESOLVING even if a mid-drain kill occurs. Skip, Wait, and Flee are each given precise semantics.

**9. Animation timing**
The `_awaitingInput` guard fully freezes `_turnTimer` — no timeout, player can think indefinitely. TURN_SPEED only governs companion/enemy auto-resolve cadence. The 200ms input-to-first-visual budget is met comfortably via the synchronous dispatch path.

Field: `gameState.combatMode: 'auto' | 'manual'`. Default `'auto'` preserves existing save behavior. One-line migration on load for saves that lack the field. The spec flags a needed audit: check whether `gs.manualCombat` at `:2585` is already persisted (if so, skip adding a new field).

Thirteen cases documented: silence during input window, stun before turn, zero mana, enemies dead before input fires, allies dying during input window, polymorph/confusion, taunt target restriction, ESC pause mid-input, screen-switch mid-turn, Wait+stun chain, companion death during input, mid-drain kill, and empty item belt.

## Key decisions and reasoning

**Section 1 — HTML/SVG grid + `&lt;img&gt;` sprites** is the pick. The Phase 01 `_computeGridLayout` sketch maps directly: give each combatant a `gridCell: {row, col}`, compute `{cx, cy, scale}` once per layout event, and apply via CSS `transform`. Canvas is eliminated from the battlefield layer entirely. Three-bullet justification: `_computeGridLayout` contract fits exactly, SVG polygons solve the overlap hit-testing problem that pixel-canvas cannot, and sprite positions only need updates on layout events not at 60fps.

**Section 2 — Coordinate formula** uses `scale = 0.85^(ROWS-1-row)` with concrete pixel outputs at 1280px wide: row 5 (companion) → 160px tiles, row 0 (back enemy) → 71.1px tiles. The vanishing point sits at 50% horizontal, 15% down from battlefield top (23% from screen top), matching Phase 00 §7's measurement.

**Section 4 — Centering fix** is `centerStartCol(count, colRange)` — a single-line formula. For 2 heroes: anchor col 1 (not 0). For 1 hero: anchor col 1. For 4 heroes: anchor col 0. `computeAnchors()` runs it for all four groups simultaneously with concrete examples in the table.

**Section 5 — Row 5 is companion** — justified by the reference image: the War Dog is visually in front of and below the standing heroes, confirming row 5 (highest index = closest to camera) must be the companion row.

**Section 12 — Per-frame cost**: current canvas path does ~70 ops/frame × 60fps = 4,200/second. New model does 0 at steady state; layout events run at most once per round boundary (~every 5 seconds). The improvement is structural, not incremental.

**Handoff to Phase 6** is at the end of the spec and defines the `gridPos` data shape, the `ev:target-select` CustomEvent payload, `activateTargeting()/deactivateTargeting()` API, and the `_layout.tileMetrics` array Phase 6 needs to size turn-strip chips at per-row depth.</result>

## What Phase 03 delivers

**25 named states** (§1), verified against all four quadrants. Every state appears in at least one transition diagram and in the surface inventory table.

**Key design decisions made:**

**State machine split.** Auto mode is a 3-node loop (`INTRO_SPLASH` → `AUTO_IDLE` ↔ `AUTO_RESOLVING` → terminal). Manual mode expands to a branching tree with 9 meaningful dwell states. The two diagrams in §2 and §3 use ASCII rather than mermaid so they remain readable in the markdown viewer without a renderer.

**Mobile is a delta, not a separate tree.** Section 4 lists 14 states that map 1:1, 3 pairs that merge into a mobile variant (`_MOBILE` suffix), and one mobile-only state (`TURN_STRIP_EXPANDED_M`). This keeps phase 10's scope bounded — it only has to solve the delta, not re-specify the whole state machine.

**`MANUAL_STATUS_LOCK`** is a named state (not just a comment). When a DoT applies Silence during the input window, the card rail cannot just go cold without explanation. The status lock state makes the rail replacement explicit, gives phase 06 a clear contract ("show status badge, no action buttons"), and gives phase 09 a tooltip trigger point.

**Three error states** (§9) follow the M383 kill-switch pattern: `ERROR_SPELL_LOAD` degrades gracefully (Basic Attack only), `ERROR_SAVE_CORRUPT` freezes combat and offers safe exit without deleting data, `ERROR_NETWORK_SYNC` is a non-blocking toast. None block player agency.

**Mode toggle as a pill, not radio buttons** (§10), because the two states are a persistent mode preference, not a form submission. The SVG sketch encodes the Hardcore locked appearance with exact token references so phase 06 can render it without guessing at opacity or color values.

**Cross-state contracts** (§6) are written as invariants rather than recommendations. The most load-bearing ones: spell rail icons stay mounted but go cold (never unmount mid-combat), turn-strip stays in DOM all round, tooltip never overlaps the active card, target picker always has a cancel path that restores `_awaitingInput`.</result>

## Key decisions made in this spec

**DOM shape.** The entire bottom HUD is a `&lt;section id="ev-hud"&gt;` replacing `#cbt-hud`. It has two rows: `.ev-hud__card-row` for heroes and `.ev-companion-row` for companions. The tooltip card is an `&lt;aside&gt;` inside `#ev-hud`, positioned at the right edge. The turn-order strip is a sibling `&lt;nav&gt;` above `.ev-battlefield`, not inside the HUD.

**Card state machine.** Five states on `data-state`: `inactive`, `active`, `resolving`, `silenced`, `dead`. State is a single attribute swap — the CSS variable overrides on `.ev-panel` handle all visual consequences (border stroke, inset glow, pulse animation) without additional class juggling. The `silenced` state applies a per-icon red overlay via `::after` on individual magic spell buttons, not on the whole card.

**Spell rail slot order.** Slot 0 is always Basic Attack (weapon-type icon from phase 08 §5). Slots 1–N are `character.skills[]` in order. Slot N+1 is Use Item. Skip is always rightmost. The item slot uses `spell-icon--enabled` (not `--ready`) because it is a free action that does not consume the awaiting-input turn.

**Click contract.** A click on a spell icon dispatches `ev:spell-pick` CustomEvent with `{characterId, skillId, targetCombatantId}`. For single-target offensive skills the rail first emits `ev:targeting-start`, calls `activateTargeting()` from phase 04, and waits for `ev:target-select` before emitting `ev:spell-pick`. For AOE-all and self-targeting heals the target is auto-resolved and `ev:spell-pick` fires immediately.

**Mobile breakpoint is 700px.** Below it, all hero cards except the selected one are `display:none`. A `.ev-mobile-portrait-strip` of up to 4 `&lt;button&gt;` elements (36×36px portrait + 8px padding = 44×44px touch target) handles switching. During `_awaitingInput`, the active actor is forced into the selected position.

**Companion row is always separate.** Companion cards have no spell rail and always show the "AI" badge. The companion card DOM does not unify with hero cards at any breakpoint.

**Rendering strategy.** Incremental dirty-check on `updateCardRail(characterId)`, matching the existing `.hm` HP-bar pattern. Full re-render only on combat start. The turn-order strip is rebuilt from scratch each round boundary (cheap, and avoids ordering bugs).

**Portrait source.** Card portrait and battlefield sprite share the same source URL. `object-fit: cover; object-position: top center` crops the face region from the full-body sprite image. No separate portrait asset is required.

**CSS class taxonomy.** 54 new `ev-`-prefixed classes introduced. All confirmed present in the preview HTML. The `.hm` family is deleted when `_renderHud` is replaced in M388/M389.

**Preview HTML.** Shows 4 hero cards (Fighter/Stormcaller/Paladin/Pyromancer) plus 1 War Dog companion card, plus the right-edge Fireball tooltip card, plus a 9-chip turn-order strip. A state selector strip at the top applies one of five states (inactive / active / resolving / silenced / dead) to all hero cards simultaneously. All phase 07 corner SVG symbols are inlined. All phase 08 spell icon SVGs are inlined. Phase 00 palette tokens drive all color.</result>

<result>I have everything I need. Here is the review.

---

**1. Label clarity — PASS with caveat**

"UI Overhaul (preview)" is honest and dev-readable. The risk: if this ever ships behind a Beta gate, "(preview)" blends into the noise of an already jargon-heavy Settings list. A slightly stronger alternative — "New Combat UI (Beta)" — mirrors how Firefox/Chrome ship behind-flag features and gives the parenthetical meaningful weight. For dev-only use the current label is fine.

**2. Hint copy — FAIL on two counts**

The milestone citation ("M390+") is fine for a developer, but it leaks internal milestone numbering to any future beta player. Replace with "future updates." More critically: the hint gives no warning that toggling mid-save may produce visual artifacts. The spec does not guarantee the new screen is applied retroactively; a player who flips it mid-dungeon-run needs to know that. Add a single sentence: "Toggling mid-run takes effect at next combat load." It also does not warn about the Auto-to-Manual round-delay rule (Phase 03 §7), which is directly affected.

**3. Toggle placement — FAIL**

The new row sits immediately after `#cbt-debug-toggle` (Combat Debugging), which is gated inside the Debug Mode group. This is the wrong neighborhood. The UI overhaul flag controls display rendering, not logging; it belongs in a Display or Beta section, not adjacent to console-output toggles. It would be less confusing after the Graphics (sprite/background toggles) group. Because Settings currently has no "Beta features" grouping, the least-friction fix is a small section divider with a "Experimental" label above the row, separated from the debug block.

**4. State affordances — FAIL (absent)**

There is no in-flight indicator that the overhaul is active. Given the entire combat screen will look different, this is important. Recommendation: a small amber pill badge — "New UI" — in the top-right corner of the Settings screen section header (or as a persistent 1-line notice at the top of the Settings panel when the flag is on). This is cheap to add and immediately answers "why does my combat screen look different?"

**5. Hardcore + mode interaction — FAIL, deferrable to M390**

The click handler at line 589–594 has zero hardcore awareness. No `disabled`, no `aria-disabled`, no lock icon, no tooltip. Phase 03 §8 fully specced all of this. However, `gameState.hardcore` is currently `false` on new saves (line 100 of gameState.js) and the flag is marked "future permadeath." No player can be in hardcore today, so this does not cause a live bug. It is safe to defer to M390 when the new combat screen actually lands, provided a TODO comment is left on the click handler referencing §8. There is already a related TODO at gameState.js:296 — a second one directly on the handler is needed.

**6. Persistence semantics — PASS**

`localStorage` is the correct tier for a UI preference flag. Per the existing pattern: per-save values (like `combatMode`, `manualCombat`) are save-file fields; UI preferences (sprite toggle, background toggle) are localStorage. The new `emberveil_ui_overhaul` key follows the established `emberveil_*` namespace convention. The `gameState.uiOverhaul` shadow-write at line 594 mirrors the same pattern used by other display preferences — no architecture debt here.

**7. Palette consumption — PASS (staged, not sloppy)**

`ev-panel.css` is self-documenting about its own intent — the file header at lines 16–18 explicitly says "Classes are intentionally unused until M389+." The tokens it consumes (`--gold-rim`, `--ember-deep`, `--ember-pit`, `--arc-blue`, `--hp-low`, `--gold-glow`, `--gold-dim`) are all defined tokens from the Phase 00 palette, not invented values. This is staged infrastructure, not dead CSS — the comment makes the intent traceable.

**8. Asset manifest UX — map_bg PASS, spell-icons PARTIAL PASS**

The `map_bg/manifest.json` is excellent — act, biome, three variants per act, a `default_variant`, and human-readable `variant_notes` explaining lighting and atmosphere for each. Any future agent can map act number to encounter type without reading the planning tree. The `spell-icons/manifest.json` is functional but thinner: `applies_to` arrays are spell-ID lists with no grouping rationale or fallback chain description. It is unclear whether `applies_to` is an exact-match list or a prefix-match, and there is no `fallback` key for "icon to use when no match found." Sufficient for M388 but will need a `fallback_icon` field and a one-line `match_rule` note before M389 wires the lookup.

---

**Top 3 recommendations for M389**

1. Move the toggle row out of the debug block into a visually separated "Experimental" section with a divider label. The debug neighborhood will confuse any player who gains access to this feature.
2. Add a visible "New UI active" indicator to the Settings panel header (amber pill badge or notice bar). Without it, the flag is forgotten immediately after toggling — players will not connect the changed combat screen to a setting they flipped.
3. Add a `fallback_icon` field and a `match_rule` comment to `spell-icons/manifest.json` before the CombatScreen wires the icon lookup. An unmatched spell ID with no fallback will either throw or silently show nothing — both are bad mid-combat.

---

**UX traps introduced by M388 (Q10)**

Two worth flagging now:

The string `"UI Overhaul (preview)"` appears verbatim in both the `aria-label` (line 334) and the `setting-label` span (line 336). If the label ever changes, it must be updated in both places — the aria-label is easy to miss. Extract to a named constant before M389 adds the combat-screen branch that may also reference this string.

The `isUiOverhaulEnabled()` function reads raw localStorage on every Settings render. Once M389 adds conditional DOM branches inside CombatScreen that also call this function, any localStorage read-timing inconsistency (e.g. a race between the click handler's write and a fast screen transition) could produce a state where the flag is "on" in Settings but "off" in the combat render cycle. The write at line 592 happens synchronously and the in-memory shadow at line 594 keeps `gameState.uiOverhaul` in sync, which is good — but the function should be documented as "localStorage is source of truth at load time; runtime source is `gameState.uiOverhaul`" to prevent a future agent from bypassing the shadow write.</result>

In The Border Roads the Shady Wandered node brought me to the Wounded Soldier node. THe Wounded Soldier node was directly in between Shady Wanderer and Emberglen, so the lines look like it connected back to Emberglen, but didn't. This is part of the "untangling nodes" update I have been working on - we need to prevent this from happening and solve the issue. Lines should avoid crossing and nodes should avoid being placed on lines between two other nodes (unless connected to both nodes). Additionally the node Ruined Watchtower branched to two nodes directly to the south, which is another overlap issue.

Game speed still does not persist across combats. It resets to 1x every time. If I change it to 4x, the next combat should start at 4x.

Change Shrines so if they are already used they act as a no-op node instead of popping up with a disabled "already used" button. However, change it so that shrines that are skipped can be revisited and activated later. Replace all shrines that restore health with a shrine that grants a random buff that lasts for the next 2+ combats: Increase XP, start combat with a shield/barrier, enemies start the roudn stunned, etc are just some examples.

Fix the Forest Warden encounter has an option where he says "you'd part coins for an old warden?" but does not actually cost any gold. Just rename that dialog so it doesn't talk about coins/gold.

I got to THornwood Forest and I see the Goblin Warrens again, that's good. However the node was directly in between Goblin Camp and Greenbough. This is another node-detanglement issue, it should not be on the path to a different node.

Change dungeons so that on any difficulty your health/mana persists between encounters. Some dungeons have a prompt like "A pit drops away, the smell is animal and old > press onward". These events are meaningless fluff that do not add gameplay, they just waste one of the dungeon "floors". Remove them. From now on, every encounter in a dungeon is combat related (but may still have text to introduce it). There should still be an occasional skill check to achieve a different outcome - perhaps a difficult skill check could let you start battle against enemies who are asleep or stunned for example, or grant a shrine buff before combat. Make all dungeon floors have at least 4 enemies and on average 6 enemies. There should be a lot of enemies, more challenge. Dungeons should be a tough challenge compared to regular nodes, to make the reward more meaningful. After combat in a dungeon the prompt for the next room appears before the victory screen is dismissed and you can see it in the background, it looks like a bug. Change so the next room prompt doesn't show until victory dialog (and subsequent dialogs) are dismissed first. This also needs to be handled for the after-dungeon message "Return to surface" prompt -> show it after I click victory and confirm who levelled up. Remove the restore hp/mp encounters within a dungeon. Goal: Dungeons are trivial right now, and I'd rather they be difficult to near impossible, specifically for a challenge.

Let's commit to the new difficulty option "Weapon Scaling". Let's make that the default and remove all the old code. Spells should not base damage off INT/STR/DEX anymore, but instead Magic/Heavy/Light damage. Also change "Melee (Heavy)" and "Melee (Light)" to "Damage (Heavy)" and "Damage (Light)" because bows also use light damage and aren't considered melee (even though melee/ranged have no actual difference in this game yet). I'd also like to do some combat simulations to compare the damage output and utility of other heroes with a balance pass to ensure all dps focused heroes do relatively similar damage ~25% deviation. Healers and tanks are accepted outside of that limit so long as their turns are spent meaningfully and not wasted. Heals and barriers are valued, overheal is waste. Overall we should find a balance between damage, mitigation, healing, and secondary buffs that affect the party. We should identify skills that underperform and list them for review on one of the tools page (or create a new "Todo List" page like the brainstorm but specifically for things I should review before being committed to the wishlist or implementation). Nevermind the download option on damage report, it can be the exact functionality as the "Save Trace" button on the combat log. But both of those buttons should turn into a smaller download icon using a floppy disk see font awesome in ..assets/

For this new round of balancing I want to focus on skills being more inline between heroes in the same class. I'd like to generate a new Damage Report tool which shows a graph of character damage per level against single or multiple targets, and solo or group of allies. You should be able to select two or more classes to compare graphs directly, I may want to compare Fighter and Warrior to see which one is more powerful against groups, for example. It would be great if this damage report stores a snapshot of benchmark data for a given milestone and in the future we can select a different milestone to compare to. The report should use combat sim results as the data, it should not actually run the combat sim on that page. Also update your own memory with instructions on how to run the combat simulations and store the results for the new Damage Report page under Tools menu. This way I can just ask "add a new set of data to the damage report for all classes", you do the rest automatically, and when pushed I can simply compare the previous milestone tot eh current milestone.

Any questions before you begin? You can work uninterrupted repeatedly releasing as many milestones as needed until the rebalance is over and damage report page is complete. You should take a snapshot of the damage report for all characters with single/aoe target grouping and solo/group party members. The damage report should also include Healing and Mitigation just like the in-game damage report, these are also useful metrics although not directly related to damage. Ideally the damage report page should let you filter heroes by their role (healer, tank, single dps, aoe dps, mabye others, just examples).

Any questions?

1. Yes that's what I meant. Single-target DPS characters should not be compared to eg Stormcaller against 6 targets because the Stormcaller is going to do LOADS more damage because of the strong AoE. AoE characters shuold ideally be very useful against multiple enemies, but less useful against single target than a solo dps. I may have mixed "class" and "category" a few times, apologies
2. Yes that sounds good and please update your memory to acknowledge its purpose and automatically maintain it when we implement features from that page. If I ever ask what to work on, you should consider the todo list, wishlist, and brainstorm
3. Sounds good except I think the max level is 20? Can we also raise the max level to 30? I actually reached max level before the last act.
4. That's OK. Enemies should have a base 3% miss chance but some enemies should have varied stats and may have more miss chance. It should not be 3% across the board, but as a baseline.
5. The "Auto" checkbox was checked at character creation, and it spent points correctly. After going to the Inventory > Attributes screen after, the Auto checkbox was disabled. So I don't think it "stuck" or is somehow wired differently. It should have stayed enabled.
- Also let's change the New Character and Hire Custom screens to have an "Auto Inventory" "Auto Passives" and "Auto Spell Talents" checkboxes at the bottom (unless manual character option is enabled in game difficultty). This way you can enable all the auto options before creating a character if you want to.
- Also let's change it so when you hire pre-made heroes from the tavern they start with their typical starting gear as if you made a new character (they currently get no items, despite a new character getting at least some white items).
- Also let's change it so when you hire a pre-made hero from the tavern a popup appears that lets you check "Auto Inventory/Attributes/Spell Talents/Passives" so that you have a chance to enable it there. That popup can be skipped entirely if manual characters are enabled in difficulty settings.
6. Ideally it would show both results on the same graph as a different color with a legend. And if you select multiple characters, it should show each character as a different color and perhaps the 1st milestone as a dotted line and 2nd as a solid line so you can easily differentiate the hero and also the milestone being compared. You should also be able to just view a single hero's graph for a single milestone. Comparing heroes or milestones is optional feature.

## Final Report

### Root Cause Analysis

**"Spells not firing" and "Blocks not firing" in actual play (CombatScreen)**: Investigation revealed **CombatScreen is correctly wired**. The enemy combatant builder (`_buildGroup`, lines 634-648) correctly copies `spellList`, `spellChance`, `blockChance`, and `blockMitigation` from the enemy data. `_enemyAI` correctly checks and fires spells at line 3568-3595. `_damagePipeline.js` correctly processes block mitigation for both heroes and enemies. The user's observation of zero spells/blocks may have been during fights where RNG didn't roll under the chance thresholds, or there was a confirmation bias issue (new spells like `bandit_flashbomb` and `shadow_blind` visually look similar to basic attacks).

**Root bugs were simulator-only:**

1. **`src/game/simulator.js` `encounterToCombatants()` lines 245-260**: Enemy combatants were built without `spellList`, `spellChance`, `blockChance`, or `blockMitigation`. All four fields were silently dropped, giving every simulated enemy `undefined` for each. This made the damage-report simulations compute as if all enemies were pure basic-attackers with no block.

2. **`src/game/simulator.js` turn loop (lines 886-898)**: Only hero AI was executed (`if (actor.kind === 'hero')`). Enemies went straight to basic attack with no spell-cast roll — zero enemy spell AI existed in the simulator.

3. **`src/game/simulator.js` block check (lines 913-916)**: Block was only applied for `target.kind === 'hero'`. A hero attacking an enemy with `blockChance` was not reducing damage. Old comment read: "enemies don't carry block stats."

### Fixes Applied

**`/home/radgh/claude/game13/src/game/simulator.js`**:
- Added `import { ENEMY_SPELLS, resolveSpells } from './enemySpells.js'` (line ~36)
- `encounterToCombatants`: Added `spellList`, `spellChance`, `blockChance`, `blockMitigation`, `skillCooldowns` fields to enemy combatant objects (lines 265-270)
- Turn loop: Added enemy spell AI block before basic attack fallback — per-turn cooldown tick, spell list check, chance roll, target selection, damage apply, and log entry emitted as `type: 'spell'` (lines 900-942)
- Block check: Changed hero-only guard to apply for all defenders; enemy branch uses `blockMitigation` percentage reduction (line 957-963)
- Hit log entry: Added `blocked: didBlock || undefined` field for tracking (line 1002-1005)

**`/home/radgh/claude/game13/src/ui/screens/CombatScreen.js`**:
- Added `window.__combatDebug`-gated `console.log` in `_enemyAI` spell-check path showing `spellList`, `available`, `spellChance`, `silenced` (lines 3573-3580)
- Added `window.__combatDebug`-gated cast log when a spell is actually fired (lines 3586-3589)

**`/home/radgh/claude/game13/src/ui/screens/_damagePipeline.js`**:
- Added `typeof window !== 'undefined' &amp;&amp; window.__combatDebug`-gated log when block fires, showing target name, blockChance, blockMitigation, raw, and post-block damage (lines 72-78)

**Path to analysis:** `/home/radgh/claude/game13/memory/damage_regression_warrior_M425_to_M469.md`

**TL;DR (3 bullets):**
- The 3.04× jump (1002 → 3049) happened in a single milestone, **M425 → M426** (commit `b72e8a811`), and is entirely a **benchmark-instrumentation change**, not a balance change. M426 rewrote the damage-report dummy to be invulnerable and zero-damage (HP ×2, dmg `[0,0]`, hit `0`) so fragile classes like Paladin/Monk could be measured without dying. Side effect: Warrior now runs the full 50-round sim window instead of dying around round 13–16, so cumulative damage scales ~3.3×.
- **Warrior class/skills/formulas are byte-identical** between M425 (`278768cba`) and M469 (`096417614`). Only `classes.js` change is cosmetic weapon-key alias renames (`2h_sword` → `sword2h`, `shield_bash` → `cleave`).
- The damage report is **measuring instrumentation, not live balance.** The Act 2+ cakewalk perception is *not* explained by these numbers and needs separate investigation (real-roster TTK benchmark, companion power creep from M427, etc.).

**Enemy HP scaling lag:** **No** — enemy HP is byte-identical between M425 and M470 snapshots (Act 1 avg 1349, Act 4 avg 1200, Act 5 avg 1480, Act 6 avg 1220). Enemies in regular acts don't scale with player level (only Infinite Dungeon does, `infiniteDungeon.js:108`). So hero-damage-vs-enemy-HP gap at L20 hasn't widened in the data — but the report falsely suggested it did.

```
Your app connects to Postgres only via a direct connection string (psql, ORMs, or an app server)
Existing tables keep their current grants. This change applies to new tables in new projects from May 30, and all existing projects from October 30.

What to do

 

For new tables you want to expose via the Data API, make explicit grants part of your table-creation flow. Without an explicit GRANT, a role will not have access to the created table.

-- Grant access per role
grant select
  on public.your_table
  to anon;

grant select, insert, update, delete
  on public.your_table
  to authenticated;

grant select, insert, update, delete
  on public.your_table
  to service_role;

-- Enable RLS
alter table public.your_table
  enable row level security;

-- Add policies
create policy "users can read their own rows"
  on public.your_table
  for select to authenticated
  using (auth.uid() = user_id);
If a grant is missing, PostgREST returns a "42501" error with the exact GRANT statement to fix it.

Rollout dates

May 30, 2026: Default for all new projects
October 30, 2026: Enforced on all existing projects
```
